lesson.summary: You arrive at her parents' door for the first time, with flowers.
body: Her mum and dad open the door. They are meeting you for the first time, so everyone is polite: they call you {{pan}} (or {{pani}}), and you call them {{pan}} and {{pani}}. With pan/pani the verb is in the third person, like talking about someone: {{Napije się pan kawy?}} is literally "Will the gentleman have a coffee?".
more: Bringing flowers for the mother (an odd number of stems, never chrysanthemums, which are for graves) is a classic first-visit gesture.
In ordinary writing, pan and pani take a small letter; a capital (Pan, Pani) is used when writing to the person, in letters and messages, as a sign of respect.

items.en: Hello! Welcome, please come in.
items.note: Zapraszamy: literally "we invite (you)", the usual way to welcome a guest.

items.pl: Dzień dobry. Bardzo mi miło panią poznać.
items.en: Hello. Very nice to meet you.
items.note: Panią: accusative of pani, "to meet you (madam)".

items.en: These are for you.
items.note: Dla + genitive: dla pani, dla pana.

items.en: What beautiful flowers! Thank you very much.

mm.pl: Dzień dobry. Miło mi wreszcie pana poznać.
mm.en: Hello. Nice to finally meet you.

mf.pl: Dzień dobry. Miło mi wreszcie panią poznać.
mf.en: Hello. Nice to finally meet you.

items.note: Wreszcie: finally, at last.

mm.pl: Mnie również. Dużo o panu słyszałem.
mm.en: Likewise. I've heard a lot about you.

fm.pl: Mnie również. Dużo o panu słyszałam.
fm.en: Likewise. I've heard a lot about you.

items.note: O + locative: o panu, o pani.

items.pl: Mam nadzieję, że same dobre rzeczy.
items.en: Only good things, I hope.
items.note: A light joke; mam nadzieję = I hope.

fm.pl: Niech pan siada. Napije się pan kawy?
fm.en: Have a seat. Would you like a coffee?

ff.pl: Niech pani siada. Napije się pani kawy?
ff.en: Have a seat. Would you like a coffee?

items.note: Napić się takes the genitive: kawy, herbaty.

items.en: Yes, I'd love one, please.
items.note: Poproszę: the polite way to accept or order something.

items.en: You have a very nice house.
items.note: Państwo: formal "you" for a couple or group, with a third-person plural verb (mają).

lesson.summary: Dinner at her parents' table: wishing everyone a good meal, praising the food, taking seconds and saying you're full.
body: Before eating, everyone says {{Smacznego!}} and the usual answer is {{Dziękuję, nawzajem.}} Her mum will keep offering more food. Say {{Tak, poproszę jeszcze trochę}} to accept, and {{Dziękuję, jestem najedzony}} (a woman says {{najedzona}}) when you really can't eat any more.
more: Refusing seconds once is often taken as politeness, so the host may offer again. A friendly, firm "dziękuję, jestem najedzony" plus praise for the food is the kind way out.
Obiad is the main hot meal, traditionally eaten in the afternoon, not in the evening.

items.en: Come to the table, everyone. Enjoy your meal!
items.note: Do + genitive: do stołu.

items.en: Thank you, you too.
items.note: Nawzajem: likewise, the same to you.

items.en: Yes, very much. They're delicious!
Did you make them yourself?
items.note: Je: "them" for things (pierogi). Sama agrees with pani.

items.en: Yes, it's my mum's recipe.

fm.en: Shall I give you some more?

ff.en: Shall I give you some more?

items.note: Nałożyć: to put food on someone's plate. Panu/pani: dative, "for you".

items.en: Yes, a little more, please.
And how about a piece of cake?
items.note: Kawałek + genitive: kawałek ciasta.

mf.pl: Dziękuję, jestem najedzony. Wszystko było pyszne.
mf.en: Thank you, I'm full. Everything was delicious.

ff.pl: Dziękuję, jestem najedzona. Wszystko było pyszne.
ff.en: Thank you, I'm full. Everything was delicious.

items.note: Najedzony: full (from eating). A woman says najedzona.

lesson.summary: Her mum calls, your partner puts her on speaker, and you get invited for Sunday lunch.
body: Your partner talks to her mum with {{ty}}, while you stay polite with {{pani}}. When her mum talks to both of you, she uses the plural {{wy}} form: {{Co robicie w weekend?}} At the end, greetings get passed on: {{Tata was pozdrawia}} and {{Pozdrów tatę!}}
more: Pozdrawiać / pozdrowić: to send greetings. Pozdrów (go, ją, tatę) is the informal "say hi to..."; formally it's proszę pozdrowić.
Do usłyszenia ("until we hear each other") is the phone version of do zobaczenia.

items.pl: Cześć, mamo! Mam cię na głośniku.
items.en: Hi, Mum! You're on speaker.
items.note: Mamo: the form for addressing mum (vocative). Mam cię na głośniku: literally "I have you on the speaker".

items.en: Hi! How are you both?
items.note: U + genitive: u was, u ciebie, u pani.

items.pl: Dzień dobry! Wszystko dobrze, dziękuję. A u pani?
items.en: Hello! All good, thank you. And you?

items.pl: Też dobrze. Co robicie w weekend?
items.en: Good too. What are you doing at the weekend?
items.note: Robicie: the plural "you" (wy), for both of you.

items.pl: Jeszcze nie wiemy. Może pójdziemy na spacer.
items.en: We don't know yet. Maybe we'll go for a walk.

items.pl: To może przyjedziecie w niedzielę na obiad?
items.en: So how about coming for lunch on Sunday?
items.note: W + accusative for days: w niedzielę, w sobotę.

items.en: We'd love to. Thank you!
Great. Dad says hello.
items.note: Literally "Dad greets you (both)".

items.en: Say hello to Dad from us!
items.note: Pozdrów: informal "say hi to"; od + genitive: od nas.

items.en: Talk to you soon!
items.note: The phone goodbye: literally "until we hear (each other)".

lesson.summary: A slow morning at home together: how you slept, coffee, and plans for the day.
body: Just the two of you, so it's all informal {{ty}}. Past tense and adjectives change with who is speaking: a man says {{jestem zmęczony}}, a woman {{jestem zmęczona}}; you ask him {{Jak spałeś?}} and her {{Jak spałaś?}} {{Kochanie}} ("darling") works for either of you.
more: Z + instrumental for "with" (z mlekiem), bez + genitive for "without" (bez cukru).
Miłego dnia! ("Have a nice day!") is in the genitive because it's short for "I wish you a nice day".

fm.en: Good morning, darling. How did you sleep?

mm.en: Good morning, darling. How did you sleep?

ff.en: Good morning, darling. How did you sleep?

mf.en: Good morning, darling. How did you sleep?

items.note: Spałeś to a man, spałaś to a woman.
Jeszcze: still.

items.en: Shall I make you a coffee?
items.note: Ci: "(for) you", the short dative of ty.

items.pl: Tak, poproszę. Z mlekiem, bez cukru.
items.en: Yes, please. With milk, no sugar.
What are you doing today?

mf.pl: Rano pracuję, a po południu jestem wolny.
mf.en: I'm working in the morning, but I'm free in the afternoon.

mm.pl: Rano pracuję, a po południu jestem wolny.
mm.en: I'm working in the morning, but I'm free in the afternoon.

ff.pl: Rano pracuję, a po południu jestem wolna.
ff.en: I'm working in the morning, but I'm free in the afternoon.

fm.pl: Rano pracuję, a po południu jestem wolna.
fm.en: I'm working in the morning, but I'm free in the afternoon.

items.note: Po południu: in the afternoon.

items.pl: To może pójdziemy razem na zakupy?
items.en: Then shall we go shopping together?
items.note: Może...? is a soft way to suggest something.

items.pl: Dobry pomysł. Musimy kupić chleb i mleko.
items.en: Good idea. We need to buy bread and milk.
I'll be back from work around five.
items.note: Około + genitive: około piątej (godziny).

items.en: OK. Have a nice day, darling!

lesson.summary: At home, you and your partner decide what to do at the weekend.
body: A relaxed chat between the two of you, all in informal ty. Notice {{Może pójdziemy…?}} ("Maybe we'll go…?"), the easiest way to suggest something, and {{Pasuje mi}} ("Works for me") for agreeing to a time.
more: {{w sobotę}}, {{w niedzielę}}: on Saturday, on Sunday. After {{w}} with days of the week, the day takes the accusative.
{{Mam wolne}} means "I have the day off", literally "I have free".
Times use the ordinal number: {{o drugiej}} (at two), {{o siódmej}} (at seven).

items.en: Are you free this weekend?
items.note: Literally "Do you have time this weekend?"

items.pl: W sobotę pracuję, ale w niedzielę mam wolne.
items.en: I'm working on Saturday, but I'm off on Sunday.
How about going to the cinema?
items.note: Literally "Maybe we'll go to the cinema?" A soft way to suggest.

items.en: Good idea! Which film?
items.note: You go {{na film}}: "to" a film uses na.

items.en: I don't know, I'll check this evening.

items.pl: A najpierw może spacer w parku?
items.en: And maybe a walk in the park first?
OK. What time are we leaving?
How about two in the afternoon?

items.pl: Pasuje mi. To ja kupię bilety.
items.en: Works for me. I'll buy the tickets, then.
items.note: {{To ja…}} = "I'll be the one who…"

items.en: Great, thank you, darling!

lesson.summary: You meet her younger brother Tomek and make small talk about work and football.
body: Siblings and people your age use informal ty straight away, so you can relax: no pan here. Notice {{Czym się zajmujesz?}} ("What do you do?"), the usual way to ask about someone's work, and {{Chętnie!}} ("Gladly!") for saying yes to an invitation.
more: {{Jestem mechanikiem}}: after {{jestem}}, a job takes the instrumental case ({{mechanik}} → {{mechanikiem}}).
Legia (Warsaw) and Lech (Poznań) are two of the best-known Polish football clubs. {{Legia z Lechem}} = Legia against Lech.
{{Tomek}} is the everyday form of the name Tomasz.

items.pl: Cześć, jestem Tomek. Wreszcie się poznajemy!
items.en: Hi, I'm Tomek. We finally meet!

mm.pl: Cześć, miło mi. Dużo o tobie słyszałem.
mm.en: Hi, nice to meet you. I've heard a lot about you.

fm.pl: Cześć, miło mi. Dużo o tobie słyszałam.
fm.en: Hi, nice to meet you. I've heard a lot about you.

items.note: Past tense ends in -łem for a man, -łam for a woman.

items.pl: Mam nadzieję, że same dobre rzeczy!
items.en: Only good things, I hope!
What do you do?
items.note: Asks about someone's job, literally "What do you occupy yourself with?"

items.en: I'm doing a PhD. And you?
items.note: Doktorat: a doctorate (PhD). Robić doktorat = to be doing a PhD.

items.en: I'm a mechanic. Do you like football?

items.pl: Tak, ale wolę oglądać niż grać.
items.en: Yes, but I prefer watching to playing.

items.pl: To może obejrzymy razem mecz w sobotę?
items.en: So how about watching the match together on Saturday?
I'd love to! Who's playing?
Legia against Lech. I'll bring beer.

lesson.summary: Christmas Eve supper with her family: sharing the wafer, exchanging wishes, and the first dishes.
body: In Poland the main Christmas celebration is {{Wigilia}}, the supper on the evening of 24 December. Before eating, everyone shares {{opłatek}}, a thin white wafer: two people each break off a piece of the other's wafer and wish each other well, then move on to the next person. Simple wishes are perfect: {{Wesołych Świąt!}}, {{Wszystkiego najlepszego!}}, {{zdrowia}}, {{szczęścia}}.
more: By tradition the meal starts when the first star appears in the sky ({{pierwsza gwiazdka}}). Children are often sent to the window to look for it.
An extra place is set at the table for an unexpected guest, so that nobody who comes that evening is turned away.

The supper is traditionally meatless, and many families aim for twelve dishes. Common ones are {{barszcz z uszkami}} (clear beetroot soup with small mushroom dumplings), {{pierogi}} (often with cabbage and mushrooms) and {{karp}} (carp, usually fried).
Wishes are in the genitive because {{życzę}} (I wish) is understood: {{(Życzę) zdrowia, szczęścia}}. {{Nawzajem}} means "the same to you".

items.en: There's the first star! We can begin.
items.note: {{gwiazdka}} = little star; the meal traditionally starts when it appears.

items.pl: Wesołych Świąt! Dużo zdrowia i szczęścia.
items.en: Merry Christmas! Lots of health and happiness.
items.note: Said while sharing the opłatek wafer.

items.en: Thank you, the same to you! All the best.
Darling, now us. Merry Christmas!

items.pl: Życzę ci zdrowia, miłości i spokoju.
items.en: I wish you health, love and peace.
items.note: {{życzyć}} + {{ci}} (to you) + the wish in the genitive.

fm.en: Thank you. May we always be together.

ff.en: Thank you. May we always be together.

mm.en: Thank you. May we always be together.

mf.en: Thank you. May we always be together.

items.note: {{byli}} when at least one of the two is a man, {{były}} for two women.

items.pl: Dla kogo jest to wolne miejsce?
items.en: Who is the empty place for?
For an unexpected guest. It's a tradition.
To start, beetroot soup with little dumplings.
items.note: {{uszka}} = "little ears", small dumplings usually filled with mushrooms.

items.en: Thank you. It smells wonderful!

lesson.summary: You visit her grandparents with flowers, ask after their health and get tea, cheesecake and a tour of the garden.
body: Use pan and pani with her grandparents: {{Jak się pan czuje?}} to grandpa, {{Czy może pani mówić wolniej?}} to grandma. They speak to you politely too, with pan (or pani), and the verb is in the third person: {{Napije się pan herbaty?}} ("Will you have some tea?").
more: {{Proszę usiąść}} ("Please sit down") is a polite, everyday formula. Older people will often press you to eat more: {{Tak, poproszę}} is always a good answer.
{{Wchodźcie}} ("come in") is plural ty, said to both of you at once.
If they suggest you call them {{babcia}} and {{dziadek}}, they are offering informal address. Until then, stay with pan and pani.

items.en: Hello! Come in, come in.

items.pl: Dzień dobry. Te kwiaty są dla pani.
items.en: Hello. These flowers are for you.
items.note: {{dla pani}}: polite "for you" to a woman.

items.en: Oh, lovely! Thank you. Please sit down.
How are you feeling?
items.note: Formal, to a man: the verb is third person.

items.pl: Nie najgorzej, tylko trochę boli mnie kolano.
items.en: Not too bad, just my knee hurts a bit.
items.note: {{boli mnie…}} = "…hurts me".

fm.pl: Napije się pan herbaty? Upiekłam sernik.
fm.en: Will you have some tea? I've baked a cheesecake.

ff.pl: Napije się pani herbaty? Upiekłam sernik.
ff.en: Will you have some tea? I've baked a cheesecake.

items.pl: Przepraszam, czy może pani mówić wolniej?
items.en: Sorry, could you speak more slowly?
Of course. Tea? And a piece of cheesecake?
Yes, please. Thank you very much.

mm.pl: A potem pokażę panu nasz ogród.
mm.en: And afterwards I'll show you our garden.

mf.pl: A potem pokażę pani nasz ogród.
mf.en: And afterwards I'll show you our garden.

items.note: {{panu}} = to you (to a man), {{pani}} = to you (to a woman).
